data.narrative:
Infleqtion is a public-stage quantum computing company founded by Dana Anderson. The valuation assessment draws from a peer set of 4 same-sector, same-stage comparables: IonQ ($13.0B), D-Wave Quantum ($6.3B), Rigetti Computing ($4.5B), and Archer Materials ($60M). This universe spans a wide range reflecting heterogeneous technical maturity and commercialization progress within the quantum sector.

The peer-median method, the sole triangulation approach applicable given data constraints, yields $5.4B. This median represents the midpoint of a distribution ranging from $60M (Archer) to $13.0B (IonQ), reflecting substantial variance in the quantum computing comp universe. Infleqtion's current valuation of $1.92B sits substantially below the peer median, positioned below the lower-quartile threshold of the identified peer set.

The triangulation analysis supports a valuation range of $4.6B to $6.2B (median $5.4B), implying Infleqtion trades at a material discount to same-stage sector peers. Key uncertainties include the heterogeneity of quantum technology approaches across comparables—spanning ion trap, superconducting, and hybrid architectures—which may limit direct comparability. The sparse single-method analysis warrants caution; additional revenue multiple, DCF, or stage-adjusted venture methods would strengthen conviction. The wide peer range ($60M–$13B) itself signals limited pricing consensus in this nascent sector.
